title: Mandol — code view
subtitle: What AgentCombo/Mandol (upstream) and the memory-bench mandol arm actually execute — P3 (tri-tower) full state is the main path; P1/P2's single dense-only path is drawn separately at B2. Lane = canonical stage; empty lanes mean the stage does not exist here.
source: repo AgentCombo/Mandol @ 6d7af4f + memory-bench @ 947c136 servers/mandol/{server.py,towers/*.py}   ·   verified against servers/mandol/verification.md (104 assertions: 80 ✓ / 5 ✗ / 16 ◐ / 3 ?, §2/§4/§5)
footer: memory-bench · methodology flow · code view · every citation re-opened and confirmed during verification
legend_notes: P1/P2 vs P3 are two different retrieval code paths, not two configurations of one path: P1/P2 (TRITOWER_ON=0) is a single space-filtered dense kNN that hard-cuts to 419 uid (conv-26), never including L1/L2 — not a ranking failure, a structural exclusion. P3 (TRITOWER_ON=1) is the full three-tower pipeline drawn below it.

The three towers (hierarchical/episodic/kg) never fuse: each runs its own internal RRF + cross-encoder rerank, but after concatenation to 75 candidates there is no cross-tower rerank or weighting. Upstream has one (a unified reranker over all 75 + a tower_separate prefilter to ~35); the adapter skips both.

Fusion:Cascade's stage3 λ=0.6 is a code default, not a paper value — the paper's Eq.(3) never gives λ a number. Stage2's arbitration score also carries a live 720h exponential time decay in every P3 query, and the cap it should respect (1500/1800/2000 tokens per script) is never wired in — it falls back to a class default of 4096 (measured: 98.0% of queries exceed 1500).

KG relations are extracted (5,208 across 10 conversations) but zero land as graph edges — a four-layer bug chain (candidate list omits entity_id, two key-name mismatches on load) confirmed against the archived run markers (kg.edges=0 for conv-41…50).
